interactions.summary: A student reads Dante's next question asking whether broken vows can be amended by other good acts.
Jiang treats Beatrice as the teacher who wants questions, then translates Dante's abstract problem into a concrete scenario where Piccarda becomes a queen and pours wealth into the poor.

Students argue that charity cannot repair Piccarda's failure because the fear at her core remains and because self-redeeming motives corrupt the act, while Jiang keeps pressing the consequentialist objection that the poor are still helped.

claims.claim: Jiang reads Beatrice as an ideal teacher who welcomes doubt and challenge because real understanding comes through questioning rather than passive reception.
Jiang frames Dante's next problem as whether spectacular later charity can redeem an earlier failure of will, using Piccarda-turned-queen as the thought experiment.
One student answer says the core issue is not the later quantity of good deeds but the unresolved fear that would return whenever the person faces the same coercive choice again.
claims.temporal_scope: Student diagnosis tested by Jiang on 2026-06-15.

claims.claim: Another student answer says self-redeeming charity fails because the deeds are not genuine gifts but instrumental acts aimed at saving oneself.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang sharpens Dante's problem into a vivid moral test by imagining Piccarda as a queen who gives all her wealth to the poor and still may not have solved the real issue.
signature_moments.source_phrase: I want to be the best queen in the world
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It turns an abstract question about vows into a memorable stress test for motive, fear, and redemption.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang keeps the room from resting in pious motive-talk by bluntly asking why motive matters if the poor are still helped.
signature_moments.source_phrase: who cares? She's still helping the poor
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It forces the packet into a live conflict between consequentialist outcomes and inner transformation.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The Dante problem of whether a broken vow can be compensated for by later good works.
Jiang's shorthand for Piccarda's surrender to fear under coercion.

chronology_notes.note: This June 15 packet opens a new stage of the discussion: the class leaves the structure of will behind and begins testing whether later beneficence can compensate for an earlier spiritual failure.
